**Visual analysis of the test image:**
- Soybean plant pulled from soil, stem split lengthwise
- **Pith is WHITE/cream-colored** — the critical distinguishing feature
- Root system is **severely blackened and rotted**, with dark, decayed lateral roots
- Stem exterior is tan/pale, no chocolate-brown discoloration

**Reasoning:**
The white pith is the definitive diagnostic feature separating **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)** from **Brown Stem Rot** (which has brown pith). The severely rotted, dark root system is consistent with SDS (caused by *Fusarium virguliforme*). The reference image confirms dark rotted roots with possible blue fungal growth in moist conditions. Phytophthora and Brown Stem Rot are ruled out by the white pith; Fusarium wilt would show brown vascular tissue extending into the stem.
